newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Finnish ERM entry unlikely this weekend - sources.
newsitem.headline: Finnish ERM entry unlikely this weekend - sources.

text.p: European Union monetary officials said on Wednesday it was unlikely that Finland would enter the bloc's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at a meeting of EU finance ministers this weekend.
Even though such a move could not be ruled out, they noted that there was already a full agenda at the informal meeting on Friday and Saturday in Dublin.
"I think there are practical considerations which should make one not expect this thing to happen in Dublin," said one monetary official. "It would be a surprise."
Finance ministers would require the help of experts who will not be present in Dublin, he added.
The meeting is due to continue vital preparations for economic and monetary union, such as discussions on a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline also after the start of monetary union in 1999.
Monetary officials said there would need to be a formal meeting about Finnish ERM membership, even if no major difficulties were expected.
They noted that the meeting of the EU's monetary committee which decided on the entry of the Austrian schilling in January 1995 lasted for some hours.
"There is a need to discuss the matter even if it is almost guaranteed that there is no reluctance for them to join," one official said.

Meanwhile, speculation is mounting on Finnish financial markets that a link is imminent, possibly in connection with the Dublin meeting. This has led to a sharp strengthening of the markka in recent days.
In a move seen as a bid to curb the gains for the currency, the Bank of Finland on Wednesday cut its key tender rate to 3.10 percent from 3.25 percent.
The Finnish government has said the country will decide this autumn whether to join the ERM or not as part of its bid to fulfill all entry requirments for the planned single currency.
